Who puts big smolts (post-smolts, 500 g and more) to sea

Take-out rate × implied growth × price — index base 100 = historical norm for that calendar month
Each series is rebased so that 100 is the average value of that same calendar month across the whole history — every June against the mean of all Junes. That strips out seasonality and puts three different units on one scale. It does not compare N to N−1: that comparison is the vertical gap between the solid curve and the N−1 curve of the same colour. Take-out above 100 while implied growth sits at or below 100 is the borrowing-from-stock configuration.
The price curve is national and does not respond to the zone filter — no price exists by production area. It is the Akvafakta monthly export value ÷ export volume, a descriptive context curve: testing showed price tracks contemporaneous harvest volume (r = −0.66 on year-on-year changes) with no usable lead from the supply ratios, so do not read it as a forecast. Gaps in the line are months with no report (May–November 2023 in particular).

Every basin, filled automatically at each news run: months with unusual deaths in each country's official data (Norway's biomass register by zone, MAST for Iceland, SEPA reports for Scotland — about six months late —, EPA mortality waste for Tasmania) and, where no data covers the month (Chile, Faroe Islands, Canada…), mortality stories taken up by the press, with the figures quoted in their titles. Events entered by hand from official statements come first and carry the cause. "Unusual" = at least twice the usual level of the zone.

      Calibre and premium, one line per year
      Harvested average weight and volume come from the Biomasseregisteret, in live weight (round weight, before gutting; gutted ≈ × 0.888). Calibre shares and premiums come from the weekly Akvafakta split (NASDAQ index up to week 18 of 2025, Sitagri after). Shares appear twice — by headcount as published, and by tonnage, which is what actually reaches the market and is always the larger figure. Premiums are the price of the 6–7 kg and of the 7–8 kg class minus the average price of 3–6 kg fish (3–4, 4–5 and 5–6 kg weighted by the tonnage sold), in NOK/kg. The 6–7 kg premium follows Norway's own big-fish supply; the 7–8 kg premium answers more to world supply and demand for large salmon. This tab is national and ignores the zone filter — no calibre or price data exists by production area.

      Compare months
      Two modes. Two months puts any two months side by side — a month against the same month a year earlier, or against the point you last took a harvesting decision. Cumulative by year adds up a chosen month range and shows one line per year, so you can read a season across the whole series rather than one pair at a time. Months still in progress carry fewer weekly reports — week counts are shown throughout so you can judge how solid each figure is.

      Exports by market
      Volume, value and realised price for the four markets Akvafakta reports monthly: China and Hong Kong, the United States, the EU27 and Japan. Everything below is rebuilt from the monthly reports each time one is added, so this tab follows the data with no manual step. Volumes are in whole-fish equivalent (WFE, round weight: fillets and other products converted back to whole fish), values are the declared export value, so the implied price mixes product formats — a market buying fillet shows a higher price per kilo than one buying whole fish. Compare movements between periods, not levels between countries.

      Product per market
      Norwegian salmon exports by destination and by product, from Statistics Norway (table 08799, monthly). Volumes are product weight — a kilo of fillet counts as one kilo, as it crosses the border — which is what makes this tab a complement to Akvafakta's round-weight figures in the Markets tab rather than a duplicate: the gap between the two tells you how processed each market's purchases are. Values are FOB, in Norwegian kroner. Recent months are provisional and are revised by SSB for up to two years; the note at the bottom says how many of the months shown are.       Zone included
      Zone excluded
      Mortality rate: cumulative mortality over the period, compounded month by month from the real monthly rates (dead/stock for each month) — not an average or a simple sum of the monthly rates. The national total compounds a national monthly rate the same way, weighted by each PO's actual headcount, month by month (not an average of the 13 zone rates). Live stock count: number of fish alive at the end of the last month of the period (not a cumulative total). All register weights are live weight (round weight: bled, not gutted — Fiskeridirektoratet's definition); gutted weight ≈ live × 0.888. Average harvest weight: total harvested weight ÷ number harvested, cumulated over the period. Average time at sea: weighted average (by number of fish harvested) of the number of months elapsed between each cohort's release and its harvest — the release month for each cohort is itself a weighted average by PO (not at the individual farm level); for cohorts released before 2017 (outside the available history), a default release month (June) is assumed. Global smolt released: all fish released into the sea under 500 g, cumulated over the period, split into < 250 g (UTSETT_SMOLT_STK) and 250–500 g (UTSETT_SMOLT_STK_MINDRE_ENN_500G minus UTSETT_SMOLT_STK — the 500 g column already contains the < 250 g fish). Fish released above 500 g are in neither column.
      Estimated post-smolt > 500 g: fish that entered the water according to the stock count (closing stock − opening stock + harvest + mortality + other losses, per zone and month) minus Global smolt released. Fish released above 500 g are in no column of the source, so this gap is the only way to see them. It is an estimate, ±5–8 M fish a year: 2018–2023 hovered between −8 and +8 M (counting errors, reporting lags), then jumped to about +25 M a year in 2024–2025, concentrated in zones 2, 3 and 4 (south-west). Transfers between zones cancel out at national level (about 1–2 M of bias). Read it on a full year, never month by month, and ignore 2022 (December 2022 releases are over-declared by ~50 M).
      Average stock weight: stock biomass ÷ headcount, at the end of the last month of the period (snapshot, like "Live stock count").
      Growth per fish (kg/month): what the fish of a zone produced in the month, all generations together — change in biomass + harvested kilos + dead fish at half weight — divided by the average number of fish, then averaged over the months of the period (the national figure weights each zone by its fish). Smolts put to sea enter at 0.15 kg and fish that vanish without being declared leave at the average weight, so neither passes for growth or loss. Unlike the former "cohort growth trend" (change in average weight), it is not pulled down when the biggest fish are harvested first. The same measure, generation by generation and against last year, is in the "Generations vs last year" tab.
      Feed consumption: cumulated over the period, in tonnes.
      Smolt weight at release: only the size band is known (< 250 g, 250–500 g). The source gives no weight or biomass at release, and nothing about fish released above 500 g.
      Source: Fiskeridirektoratet, Biomasseregisteret.
